title: Isolation of mouse brain-infiltrating leukocytes for single cell profiling of epitopes and transcriptomes
protocol: Anesthetize the mouse using methods approved by the institutional regulatory committee.
Spray chest of the mouse with water to matte down fur.
Perform a lateral incision down the center of the rib cage, cutting the skin.
Make a lateral incision through the rib cage just to the left or right of the sternum up the entire rib cage to fully expose the chest cavity.
Remove as much of the rib cage as necessary to be able to see and hold the heart with forceps.
Hold the heart steady with forceps.
Make a small incision in the right atrium.
Perfuse the mouse with 10 mL ice-cold 1× PBS without Mg2+ or Ca2+ by inserting a 25 gauge needle into the apex of the left ventricle, slowly depressing the plunger.
Cut the vertebral column/spinal cord at the base of the skull (approximately C1-C3 region) with large bone scissors to detach the skull from the body.
Insert one blade of fine scissors into the brain stem opening and brace it against the left inner part of the skull.
Snip the skull laterally from the brain stem opening until reaching the left eye, creating an ‘opening point’ on the left side and a ‘hinge’ on the right.
Push the skull cap upwards using forceps or fine scissors as an insertion/lever point to completely remove it.
Slide forceps between the bottom of the brain and skull to prop out the brain.
Place the brain in a 2 mL tube with cold 1× HBSS on ice until the next step.
Thoroughly mince mouse brain in a 2 mL tube filled with 1 mL HBSS using sharp scissors until chunks are generally small enough to be pipetted using a p1000 micropipette.
Triturate minced brain using a p1000 micropipette to dissociate it into a single cell suspension.
Transfer brain slurry contents to a 15 mL conical tube.
Use fresh 1× HBSS to wash out remaining brain slurry or fine chunks from the 2 mL tube into the 15 mL tube.
Add at least 2 mL of 1× HBSS to the 15 mL conical tube containing the brain slurry.
Centrifuge for 3 min at 300 RCF and 4°C with acceleration and brake set to low settings.
Aspirate supernatant from the brain cell pellet.
Resuspend each brain cell pellet in 2.5 mL of pre-prepared Multi-Tissue Dissociation Kit I enzyme mix.
Rotate or rock sample on a rocker or tube rotator at medium speed for 10 min at 37°C.
Triturate sample for 30 seconds to 1 minute using a p1000 micropipette, eliminating most chunks of tissue.
Any remaining chunks will be further dissociated in subsequent steps.
Rotate or rock sample at medium speed for an additional 10 min at 37°C if necessary.
Triturate sample again for 30 seconds to 1 minute using a p1000 micropipette.
Repeat the process until no tissue chunks remain.
Add at least 8 mL ice cold 1× HBSS (without Ca2+, Mg2+, or Phenol Red) to the sample.
Filter the sample through a 40 μm cell strainer into a new tube if tissue chunks remain.
Centrifuge the filtered sample for 10 min at 500 RCF at 4°C with low acceleration and brake settings.
Perform mechanical dissociation in steps 7a and 7b to ensure thorough dissociation of the tissue.
Do not replace mechanical dissociation with sonication or Dounce homogenization, as these methods could damage cells or introduce debris unsuitable for downstream experiments.
Ensure adequate mechanical dissociation to enhance enzymatic digestion effectiveness and maximize leukocyte yield.
Aspirate the supernatant from the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 3.5 mL of 70% Percoll by pipetting up and down.
Bring the total volume to 4 mL with 70% Percoll.
Layer 4 mL of 37% Red Percoll on top of the 70% layer without intermixing.
Hold the conical tube at a 45-degree angle while layering.
Slowly drip the 37% Red Percoll onto the sidewall using a p1000 micropipette.
Layer 4 mL of 30% Percoll on top of the 37% Red Percoll without intermixing.
Hold the conical tube at a 45-degree angle while layering.
Slowly drip the 30% Percoll onto the sidewall using a p1000 micropipette.
Centrifuge sample in a swinging bucket centrifuge for 25 minutes at 800 RCF at room temperature (23°C–25°C) with the acceleration at the lowest setting and no break.

Using a vacuum aspirator connected to a p1000 micropipette tip, remove layers above the buffy leukocyte layer at the interface of the 37% Red Percoll and 70% clear Percoll layers slowly, keeping the micropipette tip at the surface of the liquid.
Use a p1000 micropipette with a wide-bore tip to gently remove the remaining Percoll above the buffy leukocyte layer once within 1–2 mL of the layer.
Using a p1000 micropipette with a fresh tip, extract the buffy leukocyte layer and place it in a new 15 mL conical tube.
Bring the volume of extracted cells up to 15 mL with cold 1× HBSS (without Ca2+, Mg2+, or Phenol Red).
Centrifuge for 7 minutes at 350–400 RCF at 4°C with the acceleration and brake set to medium settings.
Aspirate supernatant from cell pellet, leaving minimal residual liquid without disturbing the cell pellet.
Take a small aliquot of cells to verify preparation consists largely of debris-free single cells and obtain a cell count.
Examine viability; proceed with subsequent steps only if cell preparation is clean, single cell suspension with >80% viability.
Centrifuge used for Percoll gradient centrifugation must be set according to indicated speed and temperature settings.
Set centrifuge for very low acceleration and no break to prevent early and late disturbances of the Percoll gradient.
Centrifuge must occur at room temperature as density of Percoll would change at lower or higher temperatures, compromising cell yield.
Once the Percoll gradient is fully layered in step 12, sample should be centrifuged within 10 minutes.
Maintain prepared gradients at room temperature before centrifugation.
Minimize amount of Percoll taken up when extracting the buffy leukocyte layer in step 15.
Resuspend cell pellet in 50 μl pre-prepared Fc Receptor block.
Incubate on ice for 20 min.
Prepare CITE-seq antibody cocktail as shown in Figure 2A.
Add 50 μl antibody cocktail to sample, pipetting up and down to mix with the sample.
Incubate on ice for 25 min.
Add at least 5 ml CITE-seq staining buffer to sample.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 350–400RCF at 4°C with medium acceleration and brake settings.
Aspirate supernatant from the cell pellet.
Resuspend in at least 5 mL CITE-seq Wash Buffer A and centrifuge for 5 min at 350–400 RCF at 4°C with medium acceleration and brake settings.
Aspirate supernatant from the cell pellet.
Resuspend in at least 5 mL CITE-seq Wash Buffer B and centrifuge for 5 min at 350–400 RCF at 4°C with medium acceleration and brake settings.
Aspirate supernatant from the cell pellet.
If multiple samples were prepared, combine individual samples in one tube.
Resuspend combined sample or individual sample in 500 μL CITE-seq Wash Buffer C and aliquot approximately 40 μL to perform a cell count.
Add at least 4.5 mL CITE-seq Wash Buffer C and centrifuge the sample for 5 min at 350–400 RCF at 4°C with medium acceleration and brake settings.
While cells are pelleting, count the aliquoted cells.
Resuspend cells in CITE-seq staining buffer at a concentration of 1,600 cells/μL for 10X superloading.
Aspirate supernatant from the cell pellet.
Add at least 5 mL Maxpar PBS to the cell pellet and centrifuge for 5 min at 350–400 RCF at 4°C with medium acceleration and brake settings.
Aspirate supernatant from the cell pellet.
Resuspend in 1 mL Maxpar PBS.
Take a small aliquot of cells to count.
Transfer an aliquot of up to 1 million cells in 100 μL or less Maxpar PBS to a new 15 mL tube.
Bring the total volume of cell suspension to 100 μL with Maxpar Cell Staining Buffer.
Add 100 μL of pre-prepared 0.75 μM Cell-ID cisplatin to the cell suspension.
Mix by pipetting.
Incubate cell suspension in Cell-ID cisplatin for 5 min at room temperature.
Add 2 mL Maxpar Cell Staining Buffer to cell suspension.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 350–400RCF at 4°C with the acceleration and brake set to medium settings.
Aspirate supernatant from the cell pellet.
Resuspend cell pellet in 50 μL pre-prepared Fc Receptor block.
Incubate on ice for 20 min.
Add 50 μL of pre-prepared antibody cocktail to sample, pipetting up and down to mix with the sample.
Incubate on ice for 25 min.
Add at least 1 mL Maxpar Cell Staining Buffer to sample.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 350–400RCF at 4°C with the acceleration and brake set to medium settings.
Aspirate supernatant from the cell pellet.
Resuspend in 150 μL Maxpar PBS and then add 150 μL 3.2% PFA.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 350–400RCF at 4°C with the acceleration and brake set to medium settings.
Incubate at room temperature for 20 min.
Add at least 1 mL Maxpar Cell Staining Buffer to sample.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 800RCF at room temperature with the acceleration and brake set to medium settings.
Aspirate supernatant from the cell pellet.
Resuspend in 300 μL pre-prepared Cell-ID Intercalator-Ir to label all nucleated cells.
Incubate at room temperature for 1 h or 4°C for 16 h.
Add 1 mL Maxpar Cell Staining Buffer to the sample.
Centrifuge the sample for 5 min at 800 RCF at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant from the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL Maxpar Water and centrifuge for 5 min at 800 RCF at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant from the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cells in 200 μL Maxpar Water and aliquot a small volume of the cell suspension to count.
Bring the total cell suspension volume up to 1 mL with Maxpar Water and centrifuge for 5 min at 800 RCF at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant from the cell pellet.
If running the sample on a CyTOF instrument immediately, resuspend cells at a concentration of 500 cells/μL in Milli-Q water containing 0.1× EQ Beads.
Seal the tube cap with parafilm and store the sample at 4°C if not using it immediately after the first wash post-Cell-ID Intercalator-Ir staining.
Partition single cells using 10× Genomics protocols.
Create a sequencing library following the 10× Genomics cell partitioning protocol.
Prepare for CITE-seq according to the CITE-seq protocol provided by 10× Genomics.
Verify the quality of cDNA libraries using a bioanalyzer, ensuring predominant peaks at ∼300–700 bp.
Check ADT library quality with a bioanalyzer, confirming predominant peaks around ∼180 bp.
Run cell suspensions on a CyTOF instrument following the most up-to-date user manual for the specific CyTOF instrument.
Acquire CyTOF data to obtain a count matrix of antibodies bound to each cell.
